mainTopic: The minimum claim for an oath (value or actual coins, partial admission or one witness), and whether admitting one of two claimed items counts as a partial admission.
overview: The גמרא continues the argument between רב, who reads the משנה's 'two silver' as a claim for value (שוה), and שמואל, who reads it as actual coins (דוקא). It tries to support רב from the gold דינר case, but רבי אלעזר says that case was a claim for 'a דינר of coins', where every coin, even a פרוטה, is the same kind. A ברייתא about a 'coined gold דינר' is also turned aside by רב אשי, and then רבי חייא brings a ברייתא that does support רב. Next, שמואל teaches that the two-מעה minimum applies only to the oath of a partial admission. A one-witness oath applies even for a פרוטה, which is learned from a פסוק and a ברייתא. שמואל also rules that if someone claims wheat and barley and the other admits to one, he must swear, and רבי יוחנן agrees. The גמרא tries to prove this ruling from the משנה about wheat and barley, but the proof is turned aside. A new attempt from the case of vessels and land begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof for the value reading from the gold dinar case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the סיפא of the משנה to prove that the claim is about value (שוה), like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is so, because the latter part of the משנה teaches: 'I have a gold דינר in your hand.' The other answers: 'You only have a silver דינר, a טריסית, a פונדיון, or a פרוטה with me.' He must swear, because they are all one kind of coin. If the claim is about value, that is why he must swear. But if the claim must be for exact coins, why should he swear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a proof for רב's view that the claim in the משנה is about value. It uses the case of a gold דינר from later in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claimant asked for gold, and the defendant admitted only silver or copper. If we look at the exact coin (דוקא), he admitted something completely different. That is not a partial admission (הודאה במקצת), so no oath should be needed. Since the משנה says he does swear, the claim must be about value: he denied part of the value and admitted part.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it is so: a word that introduces a supporting proof
The latter clause of the משנה
Value: the claim is for the worth of the coins, not the coins themselves
A gold דינר, worth 25 silver דינרים

steps.confusionAlert: Here שוה belongs to רב and דוקא belongs to שמואל. The proof is meant to support רב.

phrases.english: Know it is so, for the latter clause teaches:
'I have a gold dinar in your hand,'
'You have nothing in my hand except a silver dinar
or a tereisit, or a pundeyon, or a peruta' –
he is liable, for they are all one type of coin.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets, 'one', and some don't.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say the claim is for value –
that is why he is liable;
but if you say it means the exact coin –
why is he liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's reading of the earlier dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the claim in the משנה is for value (שוה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: a claim for a gold דינר, and an admission of a silver דינר or smaller coins, still requires an oath

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the claim was for a dinar's worth of coins
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rejects the proof. He says the case is a claim for coins worth a דינר, and the point is that a פרוטה counts as a coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: the case is where he claimed 'a דינר of coins.' The משנה is teaching us that a פרוטה is also counted as a coin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר pushes back on the proof. He reads the gold דינר case differently, so it no longer supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was not for a gold coin. It was for 'coins' adding up to a דינר. Any coin the defendant admits is the same kind of thing he was asked for, so it counts as a partial admission even under the exact-coin approach. The new lesson is that even a tiny פרוטה is called a coin.

keyTerms.meaning: A דינר's worth of coins (any coins)
It teaches us: the new point being taught

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is where he claimed from him a dinar of coins,
phrases.notes: He means coins adding up to a דינר, not one gold coin.

phrases.english: and it teaches us
that a peruta is included in the category of coin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בְּשֶׁטְּעָנוֹ בְּדִינָר מַטְבְּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by changing what the case is about.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the סיפא; it does not prove שמואל wrong
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the claim was for a gold coin. It may have been a claim for coins in general, so every coin counts as the same kind.

steps.title: The wording 'one type of coin' fits רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the wording of the משנה, 'they are all one type (מין) of coin', fits רבי אלעזר's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact this way, because it says: 'for they are all one type of coin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the words of the משנה support רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מין' (type) suggests that the claim and the admission are the same kind of item: coins. That matches רבי אלעזר, who says the claim was for coins. It also hints that even a פרוטה is that kind of item.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact this way: a support from the precise language

phrases.english: It is also precise, for it teaches:
'for they are all one type of coin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's rejection in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's reading that the claim was for coins

steps.title: How רב reads the same line
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the phrase as 'they all have one law (דין) of coin', not 'one type'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב? He reads it as: 'for they all have one law of coin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks briefly how רב explains the word 'מין', and answers right away that he reads the line as 'דין'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב the claim is about value. So the משנה is saying that all coins are treated the same in הלכה when they are used to count value. The material of the coin does not matter. This takes away the support from the wording that step 3 gave to רבי אלעזר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רב changing the text of the משנה. He is explaining what 'one kind' means: one status in halacha.

phrases.english: And Rav?
For they all have one law of coin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב against the support from the wording in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מין' means the same kind of item, which fits only a claim for actual coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means all coins share one status in halacha when counting value, which fits רב.
steps.whatToRemember: The gold דינר case does not settle the argument. רבי אלעזר reads it as a claim for coins ('מין'), and רב reads it as a claim for value ('דין').

steps.title: Must רבי אלעזר also agree with שמואל on the first clause?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since רבי אלעזר explains the סיפא the way שמואל does, does he also hold like שמואל about the רישא, 'two silver'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר: shall we say that since he explains the סיפא like שמואל, he also holds like שמואל about the רישא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks whether רבי אלעזר's reading of the סיפא forces him to agree with שמואל about the first part of the משנה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר explained the gold דינר case as a claim for actual coins, which is how שמואל reads things. The question is whether that means he also reads 'שתי כסף' in the רישא as two actual silver coins. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: introduces a suggested conclusion that may be pushed back
The first clause of the משנה (here, 'שתי כסף')

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar:
shall we say that since he explains the latter clause like Shmuel,
he also holds like Shmuel about the first clause?
phrases.notes: The first clause is the claim of 'שתי כסף', two silver מעות, in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – לֵימָא מִדְּסֵיפָא כִּשְׁמוּאֵל מְתָרֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's reading in step 2 and asks what it means for the רישא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר's explanation of the סיפא means he agrees with שמואל's exact-coin reading of the רישא

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows שמואל only in the latter clause
steps.stepSummary: No. רבי אלעזר reads only the סיפא strictly as coins, because of its wording. The רישא can be read like רב or like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Only the latter clause is meant strictly, since it says 'they are all one type of coin.' The first clause can follow רב or שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5: רבי אלעזר does not have to follow שמואל in the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר was forced to read the סיפא as actual coins only because its wording says 'one type of coin.' The רישא has no such wording. So he stays neutral there, and it can fit either רב or שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches, meaning this is the wording of the משנה
Like רב or like שמואל, meaning either view works

phrases.english: No; the latter clause is meant specifically,
phrases.notes: He means the סיפא is read strictly as actual coins, the way שמואל reads it.

phrases.english: since it teaches: 'as they are all one type of coin';
but the first clause can be like רב or like שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אלעזר also follow שמואל in the רישא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Only the סיפא is read strictly because of its wording. The רישא fits either view.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a coined gold dinar seems to support רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a claim for a 'coined gold דינר' is about a coin. The גמרא infers that a plain claim for a 'gold דינר' must be about value, like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'I have a coined gold דינר in your hand.' 'You have only a silver דינר in my hand.' He is liable. The reason is that he said 'coined gold.' So a plain claim must be about value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that a plain claim for a coin means its value, like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needed to spell out 'coined' (זהוב) for the claim to be about the actual coin. That suggests that without this word, a plain 'gold דינר' would mean just its value. This would support רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, here to take an oath
Unspecified, a plain claim with no details

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'I have a coined gold דינר in your hand,'

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵין לְךָ בְּיָדִי אֶלָּא דִּינַר כֶּסֶף״ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: 'You have only a silver דינר in my hand': he is liable.
The reason is that he said to him 'coined gold,'
but if it were unspecified, he would be telling him its value!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new proof for רב, after the discussion of רבי אלעזר ends.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that a plain claim for a coin refers to its value.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a 'coined gold דינר', read by inference.

steps.title: רב אשי: saying 'a gold dinar' is like saying 'a coined gold dinar'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the inference. The ברייתא means that even a plain 'gold דינר' counts as a coined coin, so it gives no support to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is what it means. Anyone who says 'a gold דינר' is treated like one who says 'a coined gold דינר'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes apart the proof from Step 7 so that the ברייתא can fit שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the word 'coined' being needed. רב אשי says it is not needed, since a plain 'gold דינר' already means the coin. So nothing can be learned about a plain claim being about value.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means, a rereading of the source
Is considered like, is equal to

phrases.english: רב אשי said: this is what it is saying:
anyone who says 'a gold דינר'
is like one who says 'a coined gold דינר'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the word 'coined', not the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'coined' adds something. In fact, a plain 'gold דינר' already means the coin.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ברייתא about a סלע supports רב
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches: if the claim is a סלע and he admits a סלע minus two silver מעה, he is liable. If he admits a סלע minus one מעה, he is exempt. This supports רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught in support of רב: 'I have a סלע in your hand.' 'You have only a סלע minus two silver in my hand': liable. 'Minus a מעה': exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא brings a ברייתא that supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case he denies two silver מעה, and he is liable. In the second case he denies only one מעה, and he is exempt. So what decides the case is whether the denied part reaches two silver, which matches רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Two silver, meaning two silver מעה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא's ברייתא shows that liability depends on denying at least two silver מעה, which supports רב.

phrases.english: רבי חייא teaches in support of רב:
'I have a סלע in your hand,'

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵין לְךָ בְּיָדִי אֶלָּא סֶלַע חָסֵר שְׁתֵּי כֶּסֶף״ – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: 'You have only a סלע minus two silver in my hand': he is liable;
'minus a מעה': he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in Step 7 was rejected, a new source is brought in support of רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view on the two silver of the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ברייתא: denying two silver makes him liable, denying one מעה makes him exempt.

steps.title: The two-מעה minimum applies only to partial admission, not to one witness
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the two silver מעה minimum to a case of הודאת לוה. When one witness supports the lender, a claim of even a פרוטה makes the borrower swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said in the name of שמואל: The minimum of two silver מעה was taught only when the lender claims and the borrower admits part. But when the lender claims and one witness testifies for him, even a claim of just a פרוטה makes the borrower liable to swear.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule. The minimum amount we have been discussing applies only to one kind of oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא talked about the minimum claim of two silver מעה. שמואל says this minimum belongs only to the oath of מודה במקצת. The oath that comes from one witness (עד אחד) has a much lower minimum, a single פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: This was taught only about (limits an earlier rule)
The smallest coin that counts as money in הלכה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said that Shmuel said:
They taught it only
phrases.notes: "It" is the rule from the משנה that the claim must be at least two silver מעה.

phrases.english: in a case of the lender's claim and the borrower's admission;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל טַעֲנַת מַלְוֶה וְהַעֲדָאַת עֵד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: but with the lender's claim and the testimony of one witness,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא טְעָנוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְרוּטָה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: even if he claimed from him only a peruta, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching that limits the two silver מעה minimum discussed earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two silver מעה minimum applies only to the oath of partial admission. A one-witness oath applies even for a פרוטה.

steps.title: Why is one witness different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of שמואל's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why one witness creates an oath even for a פרוטה. This sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave a rule with no source. The גמרא wants to know why the one-witness oath does not need the two-מעה minimum.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that one witness creates an oath even for a פרוטה.

steps.title: The פסוק shows one witness can create an oath
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says one witness cannot "rise up" for any sin or punishment. The גמרא learns that he can rise up to create a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or for any sin." For iniquity or sin he does not rise up, but he does rise up for an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It shows that one witness has the power to make someone swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק limits one witness only for "iniquity" and "sin", meaning punishment. The גמרא reads this to mean one witness does count for something else: obligating an oath. This step proves that the one-witness oath exists. The next step explains the פרוטה amount.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness shall not rise up (against a person)

phrases.english: As it is written:
"One witness shall not rise up against a man
for any iniquity or for any sin" —

phrases.aramaic: לְכׇל עָוֹן וּלְכׇל חַטָּאת הוּא דְּאֵינוֹ קָם,
phrases.english: it is for any iniquity or any sin that he does not rise up,
but he does rise up for an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק implies that one witness, though not enough for punishment, does obligate an oath.

steps.title: Wherever two witnesses obligate money, one witness obligates an oath
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא ties the one-witness oath to the power of two witnesses. Two witnesses obligate payment for a פרוטה, so one witness obligates an oath for a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught in a ברייתא: In any place where two witnesses obligate him to pay money, one witness obligates him to take an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to finish the proof for שמואל's rule about a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the one-witness oath follows the rules of two witnesses. Two witnesses can make someone pay even a פרוטה. So one witness can make him swear over a פרוטה, with no two-מעה minimum.
steps.whatToRemember: The two-מעה minimum belongs only to the oath of מודה במקצת. The one-witness oath follows two witnesses, so it applies even for a פרוטה.

phrases.english: And it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁנַיִם מְחַיְּיבִין אוֹתוֹ מָמוֹן,
phrases.english: Any place where two witnesses obligate him to pay money,
phrases.notes: Two witnesses can obligate payment even for a פרוטה, so the same is true here.

phrases.english: one witness obligates him to take an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁנַיִם מְחַיְּיבִין אוֹתוֹ מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that explains the פרוטה amount, completing the answer of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a one-witness oath applies even for a פרוטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא linking one witness's oath to two witnesses' power to obligate money.

steps.title: Claimed wheat and barley, admitted one: he must swear
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if someone claims wheat and barley and the defendant admits to one of them, this counts as partial admission and he must swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: If he claimed wheat and barley from him, and he admitted to one of them, he is liable to swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, separate ruling of שמואל about partial admission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think wheat and barley are two separate claims, so admitting one is a full admission of that claim and a full denial of the other. שמואל says they are one combined claim. Admitting one type is admitting part of the claim, so he swears.

keyTerms.meaning: He admitted to him one of them

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
If he claimed wheat and barley from him,
and he admitted to him one of them, he is liable.
phrases.notes: "Liable" means he must take the oath of someone who admits part of a claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: טְעָנוֹ חִטִּין וּשְׂעוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling of שמואל, unrelated to the one-witness topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A claim of two kinds with admission to one kind counts as partial admission, so he must swear.

steps.title: רבי יצחק praises the ruling and says רבי יוחנן agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says שמואל's ruling is correct and that רבי יוחנן said the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said to him: Well said, and so said רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק backs up שמואל's ruling by saying רבי יוחנן held the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds the support of a major אמורא from ארץ ישראל. Because רבי יצחק mentions only רבי יוחנן, it sets up the next question about ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said to him:
Well said, and so said Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִצְחָק: יִישַׁר, וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling on wheat and barley.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's matching statement, reported by רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Did ריש לקיש disagree?
steps.stepSummary: Since only רבי יוחנן was mentioned, the גמרא asks whether ריש לקיש disagreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that ריש לקיש disagreed with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that ריש לקיש, who often argues with רבי יוחנן, is not mentioned. It asks whether he held differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting only רבי יוחנן might hint that his usual partner in debate, ריש לקיש, disagreed. The גמרא checks whether that conclusion is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this imply that he disagrees?
The study partner of רבי יוחנן, who often argues with him

phrases.english: By implication, does Reish Lakish disagree with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible inference from the fact that step 15 mentions only רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ריש לקיש disagreed with רבי יוחנן on this ruling.

steps.title: ריש לקיש was silent, either waiting or drinking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the inference is not proven. ריש לקיש simply said nothing at the time, and two versions explain why: he was waiting, or he was drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: He was waiting and stayed silent. Others say: He was drinking and stayed silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש is not mentioned only because he said nothing at that time. It gives two reasons for his silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence was not a disagreement. In one version he was holding back, waiting for רבי יוחנן to finish. In the other he was busy drinking. Either way, nothing shows that he argued.
steps.confusionAlert: The two Aramaic versions sound almost the same (שָׁהֵי "waiting" and שָׁתֵי "drinking"). They differ by one letter, so read carefully.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: מִישְׁהָא הֲוָה שָׁהֵי לֵיהּ וְשָׁתֵיק לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: he was waiting and stayed silent,
phrases.notes: He held back until רבי יוחנן finished, so we never heard his view.

phrases.english: and there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: מִישְׁתָּא הֲוָה שָׁתֵי לֵיהּ וּשְׁתֵיק לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: he was drinking and stayed silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מִישְׁהָא הֲוָה שָׁהֵי לֵיהּ וְשָׁתֵיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16: ריש לקיש's silence was not a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש did not express an opinion. He was silent because he was either waiting or drinking.

steps.title: A possible proof for שמואל from the wheat-and-barley משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if someone claims wheat and the defendant admits to barley, the defendant is exempt. The גמרא reads into this: the reason is that only wheat was claimed. So if both wheat and barley were claimed and he admitted to one, he would be liable, just as שמואל says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say the משנה supports שמואל. It says: if he claimed wheat and the defendant admitted to barley, he is exempt, and רבן גמליאל makes him liable. The reason he is exempt is that the claim was only wheat and the admission was barley. That implies that if the claim was wheat and barley and he admitted to one of them, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove שמואל's ruling from step 14 by reading a hidden implication out of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא exempts the defendant only because his admission (barley) is a different item from the claim (wheat). The גמרא infers that if barley had also been part of the claim, admitting to it would count as partial admission. That is exactly שמואל's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
The reason is X, but otherwise... (reading an implication out of a text)

phrases.english: Let us say [the משנה] supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is שמואל, who ruled in step 14 that admitting to one of two items requires an oath.

phrases.aramaic: טְעָנוֹ חִטִּין וְהוֹדָה לוֹ בִּשְׂעוֹרִין – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: If he claimed wheat from him and he admitted to him barley, he is exempt.
And רבן גמליאל makes him liable.
The reason is that he claimed wheat
and he admitted to him barley;
but [if he claimed] wheat and barley
and he admitted to him one of them, he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After confirming that רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל, the גמרא looks for support for שמואל in the משנה itself.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a claim of wheat and barley with admission to one counts as partial admission
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of a claim of wheat with admission to barley, read through 'the reason is... but otherwise'

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the משנה's case shows רבן גמליאל's strength
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the inference is not forced. Even with a claim of wheat and barley, the תנא קמא might exempt him. The משנה chose the case of wheat alone to show how far רבן גמליאל goes: he obligates an oath even when the admission is a completely different item.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The same law could apply, so that even with wheat and barley he is also exempt. The reason they argue about a claim of wheat alone is to show you how far רבן גמליאל's opinion goes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from step 18 by giving another reason the משנה picked its case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the case being chosen to limit the תנא קמא's exemption. The גמרא says the case was chosen for רבן גמליאל instead: he obligates an oath even when the admitted item was never claimed. So nothing can be learned about wheat-and-barley claims, and שמואל gets no support here.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength (how far an opinion goes)

steps.confusionAlert: "The strength of רבן גמליאל" does not mean the תנא קמא agrees with him. It means the משנה picked the most extreme case, one where even רבן גמליאל's ruling is surprising, to show how far his view of liability goes.

phrases.english: No; the same law applies
that even [with a claim of] wheat and barley he is also exempt;
and the fact that they argue about [a claim of] wheat
is to show you the strength of רבן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה only, not שמואל's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's choice of case can be explained as showing רבן גמליאל's strength, so the implied rule about wheat and barley is not forced.

steps.title: A second attempt: the משנה about vessels and land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another line from the משנה. If someone claims vessels and land, and the defendant admits to one and denies the other, he is exempt. The inference for שמואל is drawn from this on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he claimed vessels and land from him, and the defendant admitted to the vessels and denied the land, or admitted to the land and denied the vessels, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to support שמואל by quoting another case from the משנה. This step only sets up the case; the inference comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like שמואל's case, this is a claim of two different items with an admission to only one. Here the משנה says he is exempt. The גמרא will now look at why he is exempt, to see whether it implies something about שמואל's case.

phrases.english: Come and hear: if he claimed vessels and land from him;
[and] he admitted to the vessels and denied the land,
[or admitted] to the land and denied the vessels, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a different case from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling about a claim of two different items
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of a claim of vessels and land (the inference follows on the next amud)
